filing.overview: Alphabet is a collection of businesses, the largest of which is Google. Google reports two segments, Google Services and Google Cloud, and non-Google businesses are grouped as Other Bets.

areas.name: Google Services advertising
areas.description: Performance and brand advertising on Google Search and other properties, YouTube, and Google Network partner sites, sold to advertisers, agencies, and publishers. The text names no specific competitors for this line.

quotes.text: Google Services generates revenues primarily by delivering both performance and brand advertising that appears on Google Search & other properties, YouTube, and Google Network partners' properties

areas.name: Consumer subscriptions
areas.description: Paid subscriptions, mainly YouTube services such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, and NFL Sunday Ticket, plus Google One, which offers access to the most capable Gemini models.

quotes.text: consumer subscriptions, which primarily include revenues from YouTube services, such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, and NFL Sunday Ticket, as well as Google One, which offers access to our most capable Gemini models;

areas.name: Google Cloud
areas.description: Cloud infrastructure, AI development platform, cybersecurity, data analytics, and agent offerings such as Gemini Enterprise, sold through fees and subscriptions. Competitors are named only generally, as enterprise cloud providers.

quotes.text: Through our Google Cloud Platform and Google Workspace offerings, Google Cloud generates revenues primarily from consumption-based fees and subscriptions for infrastructure, platform, applications, and other cloud services.

areas.name: Other Bets
areas.description: Non-Google businesses at various stages, such as Waymo for autonomous ride-hailing and the X moonshot unit. Revenue comes mainly from autonomous transportation and internet services.

quotes.text: Revenues from Other Bets are generated primarily from the sale of autonomous transportation and internet services.
our fully autonomous driving technology company, Waymo, is now providing fully autonomous, paid ride-hailing services to customers in multiple cities

risks.summary: Most revenue comes from online advertising, and advertisers and partners can end contracts at any time. Shifts in ad formats, ad blocking, and privacy changes could reduce revenue.

quotes.text: We generated more than 70% of total revenues from online advertising in 2025. Many of our advertisers, companies that distribute our products and services, digital publishers, and content providers can terminate their contracts with us at any time.

risks.summary: The company faces many competitors, from large incumbents to start-ups, including AI developers. It must keep innovating or risk losing users, advertisers, and customers.

quotes.text: Our business environment is rapidly evolving and intensely competitive. Our businesses face changing technologies, shifting user needs, and frequent introductions of rival products and services.

risks.summary: Large spending on AI infrastructure, leases, and long-term commitments raises costs and liabilities. Dependence on third-party equipment and capacity adds further exposure.

quotes.text: To meet the compute capacity demands of AI training and inference, as well as traditional cloud computing services, we are entering into significant leasing arrangements with third party operators, which may increase costs and operational complexity.

risks.summary: The company faces multiple US antitrust lawsuits covering advertising technology, Search, and Android and Play Store. Remedies could restrict distribution and business practices, and new laws worldwide add compliance costs.

quotes.text: The US Department of Justice (DOJ), various states, and other plaintiffs have filed, and may continue to file in the future, several antitrust lawsuits about aspects of our business, including our advertising technologies and practices, the operation and distribution of Google Search, and the operation and distribution of Android operating system and Play Store.

risks.summary: Privacy and data laws are complex and changing, and AI training on user data draws scrutiny. Failure to comply could bring fines, orders to change practices, and reputational harm.

quotes.text: Privacy, data protection, data usage, and portability regulations are complex and rapidly evolving areas. Any failure or alleged failure to comply with these laws could harm our business, reputation, financial condition, and operating results.

risks.summary: The company faces cyber attacks on a regular basis, including nation-state threats, and AI may increase these risks. A breach could cause legal exposure and loss of user trust.

quotes.text: We experience cyber attacks and other attempts to gain unauthorized access to our systems on a regular basis. Cyber attacks continue to evolve in sophistication and volume, and inherently may be difficult to detect for long periods of time.

risks.summary: Growth is limited by power, water, and land, and specialized AI chips come from a small number of suppliers. Devices depend on contract manufacturers and some single-source components.

quotes.text: Our ability to scale our technical infrastructure is increasingly constrained by the availability of power, water, and land. For example, energy supply is constrained globally due to the significant increase in demand for and limited availability of energy to power AI compute.

risks.summary: AI products may produce harmful content, inaccuracies, or infringe rights, and the company may not catch all issues. This could bring regulatory action, liability, and reputational harm.

quotes.text: Our evolving AI-enabled products and services may give rise to risks related to harmful content, inaccuracies, discrimination, intellectual property infringement or misappropriation, violation of rights of publicity, defamation, data privacy, cybersecurity, minor protection, and other issues.

risks.summary: A large share of revenue comes from outside the US, exposing the company to sanctions, tariffs, geopolitical conflict, foreign exchange swings, and varied local laws.

quotes.text: Our international operations are significant to our revenues and net income, and we plan to continue growing internationally. International revenues accounted for approximately 52% of consolidated revenues in 2025.

risks.summary: Larry Page and Sergey Brin hold a majority of the voting power through Class B stock, which limits other stockholders' influence over corporate matters, including a sale of the company.

quotes.text: Through their stock ownership, Larry and Sergey have significant influence over all matters requiring stockholder approval, including the election of directors and significant corporate transactions, such as a merger or other sale of our company or our assets, for the foreseeable future.

filing.overview: Meta Platforms builds social apps (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads, WhatsApp, Meta AI) that earn substantially all revenue from advertising, and develops VR headsets and AI glasses through its Reality Labs segment.

areas.name: Family of Apps advertising
areas.description: Sells ad placements on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads, WhatsApp, and third-party apps to marketers via self-service tools, a sales force, agencies, and resellers. Competes with companies that sell advertising and with companies that help users share and discover content.

quotes.text: Currently, we generate substantially all of our revenue from selling advertising placements on our family of apps to marketers, which is reflected in FoA.

We face significant competition in every aspect of our business, including, but not limited to, companies that facilitate the ability of users to create, share, communicate, and discover content and information online or enable marketers to reach their existing or prospective audiences.

areas.name: Messaging and social apps
areas.description: WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads let people communicate privately and share public updates. Revenue is mainly from ads and business messaging is described as limited; competitors are described only generally as companies offering communication and sharing products.

quotes.text: WhatsApp is a simple, reliable, and secure messaging application that is used by people and businesses around the world to communicate and transact in a private way.

areas.name: Reality Labs consumer hardware and software
areas.description: Sells Meta Quest VR devices, Meta Horizon Store content, and Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta AI glasses through retailers, resellers, distribution partners, and Meta.com. Competes in consumer hardware and AR and VR products.

quotes.text: RL generates revenue from sales of consumer hardware products, software, and content.

We also compete with companies in the development and application of AI, particularly with respect to the development of frontier AI models, as well as the development and delivery of consumer hardware and augmented and virtual reality products and services.

areas.name: Meta AI and AI models
areas.description: Meta AI assistant available across apps, as a stand-alone app, on AI glasses, and on the web, plus Llama and other models, some released as open source. Competes with companies developing frontier AI models and AI features.

quotes.text: We have a history of open-sourcing in AI, including releasing our Llama foundation models as well as other models and tools, and continue to believe in the power of open source innovation.
Meta AI is an assistant that's available across our apps, as a stand-alone app, on our AI glasses, and on the web.

risks.summary: Substantially all revenue comes from advertising, so declines in users, engagement, or marketer spending would reduce revenue. Marketers have no long-term commitments.

quotes.text: We generate substantially all of our revenue from advertising. The loss of marketers, or reduction in spending by marketers, could seriously harm our business.
If we fail to retain existing users or add new users, or if our users decrease their level of engagement with our products, our revenue, financial results, and business may be significantly harmed.

risks.summary: Changes by Apple, Google, privacy regulators, and Meta's own products limit the data used for ad targeting and measurement, which has hurt advertising revenue.

quotes.text: Our ad targeting and measurement tools rely on data signals from user activity on websites and services that we do not control, as well as signals generated within our products, in order to deliver relevant and effective ads to our users, and any changes in our ability to use such signals will adversely affect our business.

In addition, mobile operating system and browser providers, such as Apple and Google, have implemented product changes and/or announced plans to limit the ability of websites and application developers to collect and use these signals to target and measure advertising.

risks.theme: Reality Labs and AI investment returns
risks.summary: Heavy spending on Reality Labs, AI, and infrastructure reduces operating margin, and these investments may not pay off. Reality Labs is expected to keep operating at a loss.

quotes.text: For example, our investments in Reality Labs reduced our 2025 overall operating profit by approximately $19.19 billion, and we expect our 2026 Reality Labs operating losses to remain similar to 2025.
We may not be successful in our artificial intelligence initiatives, which could adversely affect our business, reputation, or financial results.

risks.summary: Privacy, content, competition, and youth-protection laws in the US, EU, and elsewhere could force product changes, fines, or limits on advertising, including an FTC consent order and EU rules on ad models.

quotes.text: Our business is subject to complex and evolving U.S. and foreign laws and regulations regarding privacy, data use, data combination, data protection, content, AI, competition, youth, safety, consumer protection, advertising, e-commerce, and other matters.

risks.summary: Meta faces numerous class actions and government suits, including youth-related, privacy, antitrust, copyright, and securities claims, which could lead to large damages or required changes.

quotes.text: We are involved in numerous class action lawsuits and other litigation matters that are expensive and time consuming, and, if resolved adversely, could harm our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

We are currently, and expect to be in the future, party to patent, trademark, and copyright lawsuits and other intellectual property rights claims that are expensive and time consuming and, if resolved adversely, could have a significant impact on our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

risks.summary: Meta is a prominent target for cyber-attacks and misuse of user data, and AI tools add new vulnerabilities.

quotes.text: Security breaches, improper access to or disclosure of our data or user data, other hacking and phishing attacks on our systems, or other cyber incidents could harm our reputation and adversely affect our business.

risks.summary: Meta depends on third-party data center services and a small number of component manufacturers, often concentrated in Asia, for technical infrastructure and consumer hardware.

quotes.text: A substantial portion of our technical infrastructure is provided by third parties. Any disruption or failure in the services we receive from these providers could harm our ability to handle existing or increased traffic and could significantly harm our business.
The manufacturing of our consumer hardware products depends on a small number of third parties, often with significant operations in a single region such as Asia.

risks.summary: Meta faces competition for users, marketers, developers, and AI talent from many companies, some with greater resources, and platform owners such as Apple and Google can favor their own products.

quotes.text: Some of our current and potential competitors may have greater resources, experience, or stronger competitive positions in certain product segments, geographic regions, or user demographics than we do.
For example, each of Apple and Google have integrated competitive products with iOS and Android, respectively.

risks.summary: Mark Zuckerberg controls a majority of voting power through Class B shares, so Class A holders have limited influence over corporate matters.

quotes.text: This concentrated control will limit or preclude your ability to influence corporate matters for the foreseeable future.

items: Both companies sell advertising and both build AI products, which is where the filings overlap most directly.
Alphabet also reports Google Cloud, consumer subscriptions and Other Bets such as Waymo. Meta's filing describes none of these.

Meta describes substantially all of its revenue as coming from advertising. It also reports Reality Labs hardware, including VR headsets and AI glasses, which Alphabet's business description does not list.
FY2025 revenue was $402.8B for Alphabet and $201.0B for Meta. Their R&D was $61.1B and $57.4B.
Long-term debt rose at both companies in FY2025, to $46.5B at Alphabet and $58.7B at Meta.

html:
Both companies earn mainly from advertising and compete in AI; beyond that, their other lines diverge.

Business overlap

Rows follow each 10-K's business areas (Item 1); overlap is shown only as the filings describe it.

MarketGOOGLMETA
Online advertisingBoth serve advertisers and marketers.ServesSearch, YouTube, Network partnersServesFacebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads, WhatsApp, third-party apps
AI models and assistantsBoth name AI development and competition in it.ServesGemini models via Google One; AI platform in CloudServesMeta AI, Llama (some open source)
Cloud infrastructure and enterprise softwareServesGoogle Cloud Platform, WorkspaceNot covered
Consumer subscriptionsServesYouTube TV, Music, Premium, NFL Sunday Ticket, Google OneNot covered
Autonomous transportation, Other BetsServesWaymo ride-hailing, XNot covered
Consumer hardware, VR and AI glassesNot covered as a segmentServesReality Labs: Quest, Horizon Store, Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta
Messaging appsNot listedServesWhatsApp, Messenger, Threads

Revenue

Scale across FY2021 to FY2025.

R&D % of revenue

Reinvestment relative to size.

R&D spend

Absolute R&D by year.

Operating margin

By year.

Takeaways

  • Both filings describe advertising as the core revenue line: Alphabet more than 70% of 2025 revenue, Meta substantially all.
  • Alphabet lists cloud, subscriptions and Other Bets that Meta's filing does not; Meta lists Reality Labs hardware and messaging apps.
  • Both describe AI development, Meta with Llama and Meta AI, Alphabet with Gemini.
  • FY2025 revenue was $402.8B for GOOGL and $201.0B for META, while R&D was $61.1B and $57.4B.

Not financial advice. Source: each company's 10-K filings, FY2021 to FY2025. Gross profit and gross margin are n/r.

prompt.system:
You build a comparison of two public companies by calling UI component tools. The page already shows each company's name, industry and headquarters and, above your components, a headline strip of each company's latest-year Revenue, R&D, R&D % of revenue, Operating margin: don't repeat those latest-year values as metric cards (trends and other years are fine).

Lens: Where do the two businesses overlap, and where do they not?
Built from each company's 10-K business description (the business areas listed for each company). business_overlap is the core: one component with a row for every market, those both serve and each company's ground the other doesn't cover. Revenue and R&D can add scale. Describe overlap only as the filings state it; never infer market share.

Rules:
- Respond only through tool calls, in the order the reader should see them: usually 3 to 6 components, at most 8, then takeaways last. When takeaways succeeds, reply "done".
- Components take metric keys and fiscal years, never numbers, and annual-report ids (AAPL-r2), never quotes. The page looks every value and quote up and cites its filing.
- Takeaways are neutral differences, never a winner, a recommendation or a prediction. Any number you write must appear in the data tables exactly as shown.
- "n/r" means the filing does not report it and "n/m" means the ratio is not meaningful (e.g. negative equity). Never estimate around them; say they are not reported when it matters.
- The two companies may have different fiscal year ends; "latest" picks each company's own latest year.
- If a tool returns an error, fix the call and try again.

GOOGL annual report (10-K for FY2025): Alphabet is a collection of businesses, the largest of which is Google. Google reports two segments, Google Services and Google Cloud, and non-Google businesses are grouped as Other Bets.
Business areas:
GOOGL-a1 | Google Services advertising | Performance and brand advertising on Google Search and other properties, YouTube, and Google Network partner sites, sold to advertisers, agencies, and publishers. The text names no specific competitors for this line.
  "Google Services generates revenues primarily by delivering both performance and brand advertising that appears on Google Search & other properties, YouTube, and Google Network partners' properties" (Item 1)
GOOGL-a2 | Consumer subscriptions | Paid subscriptions, mainly YouTube services such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, and NFL Sunday Ticket, plus Google One, which offers access to the most capable Gemini models.
  "consumer subscriptions, which primarily include revenues from YouTube services, such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, and NFL Sunday Ticket, as well as Google One, which offers access to our most capable Gemini models;" (Item 1)
GOOGL-a3 | Google Cloud | Cloud infrastructure, AI development platform, cybersecurity, data analytics, and agent offerings such as Gemini Enterprise, sold through fees and subscriptions. Competitors are named only generally, as enterprise cloud providers.
  "Through our Google Cloud Platform and Google Workspace offerings, Google Cloud generates revenues primarily from consumption-based fees and subscriptions for infrastructure, platform, applications, and other cloud services." (Item 1)
GOOGL-a4 | Other Bets | Non-Google businesses at various stages, such as Waymo for autonomous ride-hailing and the X moonshot unit. Revenue comes mainly from autonomous transportation and internet services.
  "Revenues from Other Bets are generated primarily from the sale of autonomous transportation and internet services." (Item 1)
  "our fully autonomous driving technology company, Waymo, is now providing fully autonomous, paid ride-hailing services to customers in multiple cities" (Item 1)
Risk themes:
GOOGL-r1 | Advertising dependence | Most revenue comes from online advertising, and advertisers and partners can end contracts at any time. Shifts in ad formats, ad blocking, and privacy changes could reduce revenue.
  "We generated more than 70% of total revenues from online advertising in 2025. Many of our advertisers, companies that distribute our products and services, digital publishers, and content providers can terminate their contracts with us at any time." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r2 | Competition | The company faces many competitors, from large incumbents to start-ups, including AI developers. It must keep innovating or risk losing users, advertisers, and customers.
  "Our business environment is rapidly evolving and intensely competitive. Our businesses face changing technologies, shifting user needs, and frequent introductions of rival products and services." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r3 | Infrastructure costs and AI capacity | Large spending on AI infrastructure, leases, and long-term commitments raises costs and liabilities. Dependence on third-party equipment and capacity adds further exposure.
  "To meet the compute capacity demands of AI training and inference, as well as traditional cloud computing services, we are entering into significant leasing arrangements with third party operators, which may increase costs and operational complexity." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r4 | Antitrust and regulation | The company faces multiple US antitrust lawsuits covering advertising technology, Search, and Android and Play Store. Remedies could restrict distribution and business practices, and new laws worldwide add compliance costs.
  "The US Department of Justice (DOJ), various states, and other plaintiffs have filed, and may continue to file in the future, several antitrust lawsuits about aspects of our business, including our advertising technologies and practices, the operation and distribution of Google Search, and the operation and distribution of Android operating system and Play Store." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r5 | Privacy and data protection | Privacy and data laws are complex and changing, and AI training on user data draws scrutiny. Failure to comply could bring fines, orders to change practices, and reputational harm.
  "Privacy, data protection, data usage, and portability regulations are complex and rapidly evolving areas. Any failure or alleged failure to comply with these laws could harm our business, reputation, financial condition, and operating results." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r6 | Cybersecurity | The company faces cyber attacks on a regular basis, including nation-state threats, and AI may increase these risks. A breach could cause legal exposure and loss of user trust.
  "We experience cyber attacks and other attempts to gain unauthorized access to our systems on a regular basis. Cyber attacks continue to evolve in sophistication and volume, and inherently may be difficult to detect for long periods of time." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r7 | Power, supply chain, and hardware | Growth is limited by power, water, and land, and specialized AI chips come from a small number of suppliers. Devices depend on contract manufacturers and some single-source components.
  "Our ability to scale our technical infrastructure is increasingly constrained by the availability of power, water, and land. For example, energy supply is constrained globally due to the significant increase in demand for and limited availability of energy to power AI compute." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r8 | AI product risks | AI products may produce harmful content, inaccuracies, or infringe rights, and the company may not catch all issues. This could bring regulatory action, liability, and reputational harm.
  "Our evolving AI-enabled products and services may give rise to risks related to harmful content, inaccuracies, discrimination, intellectual property infringement or misappropriation, violation of rights of publicity, defamation, data privacy, cybersecurity, minor protection, and other issues." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r9 | International operations | A large share of revenue comes from outside the US, exposing the company to sanctions, tariffs, geopolitical conflict, foreign exchange swings, and varied local laws.
  "Our international operations are significant to our revenues and net income, and we plan to continue growing internationally. International revenues accounted for approximately 52% of consolidated revenues in 2025." (Item 1A)
GOOGL-r10 | Founder control | Larry Page and Sergey Brin hold a majority of the voting power through Class B stock, which limits other stockholders' influence over corporate matters, including a sale of the company.
  "Through their stock ownership, Larry and Sergey have significant influence over all matters requiring stockholder approval, including the election of directors and significant corporate transactions, such as a merger or other sale of our company or our assets, for the foreseeable future." (Item 1A)

META annual report (10-K for FY2025): Meta Platforms builds social apps (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads, WhatsApp, Meta AI) that earn substantially all revenue from advertising, and develops VR headsets and AI glasses through its Reality Labs segment.
Business areas:
META-a1 | Family of Apps advertising | Sells ad placements on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads, WhatsApp, and third-party apps to marketers via self-service tools, a sales force, agencies, and resellers. Competes with companies that sell advertising and with companies that help users share and discover content.
  "Currently, we generate substantially all of our revenue from selling advertising placements on our family of apps to marketers, which is reflected in FoA." (Item 1)
  "We face significant competition in every aspect of our business, including, but not limited to, companies that facilitate the ability of users to create, share, communicate, and discover content and information online or enable marketers to reach their existing or prospective audiences." (Item 1)
META-a2 | Messaging and social apps | WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads let people communicate privately and share public updates. Revenue is mainly from ads and business messaging is described as limited; competitors are described only generally as companies offering communication and sharing products.
  "WhatsApp is a simple, reliable, and secure messaging application that is used by people and businesses around the world to communicate and transact in a private way." (Item 1)
META-a3 | Reality Labs consumer hardware and software | Sells Meta Quest VR devices, Meta Horizon Store content, and Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta AI glasses through retailers, resellers, distribution partners, and Meta.com. Competes in consumer hardware and AR and VR products.
  "RL generates revenue from sales of consumer hardware products, software, and content." (Item 1)
  "We also compete with companies in the development and application of AI, particularly with respect to the development of frontier AI models, as well as the development and delivery of consumer hardware and augmented and virtual reality products and services." (Item 1)
META-a4 | Meta AI and AI models | Meta AI assistant available across apps, as a stand-alone app, on AI glasses, and on the web, plus Llama and other models, some released as open source. Competes with companies developing frontier AI models and AI features.
  "We have a history of open-sourcing in AI, including releasing our Llama foundation models as well as other models and tools, and continue to believe in the power of open source innovation." (Item 1)
  "Meta AI is an assistant that's available across our apps, as a stand-alone app, on our AI glasses, and on the web." (Item 1)
Risk themes:
META-r1 | Advertising dependence and user engagement | Substantially all revenue comes from advertising, so declines in users, engagement, or marketer spending would reduce revenue. Marketers have no long-term commitments.
  "We generate substantially all of our revenue from advertising. The loss of marketers, or reduction in spending by marketers, could seriously harm our business." (Item 1A)
  "If we fail to retain existing users or add new users, or if our users decrease their level of engagement with our products, our revenue, financial results, and business may be significantly harmed." (Item 1A)
META-r2 | Data signals and platform changes | Changes by Apple, Google, privacy regulators, and Meta's own products limit the data used for ad targeting and measurement, which has hurt advertising revenue.
  "Our ad targeting and measurement tools rely on data signals from user activity on websites and services that we do not control, as well as signals generated within our products, in order to deliver relevant and effective ads to our users, and any changes in our ability to use such signals will adversely affect our business." (Item 1A)
  "In addition, mobile operating system and browser providers, such as Apple and Google, have implemented product changes and/or announced plans to limit the ability of websites and application developers to collect and use these signals to target and measure advertising." (Item 1A)
META-r3 | Reality Labs and AI investment returns | Heavy spending on Reality Labs, AI, and infrastructure reduces operating margin, and these investments may not pay off. Reality Labs is expected to keep operating at a loss.
  "For example, our investments in Reality Labs reduced our 2025 overall operating profit by approximately $19.19 billion, and we expect our 2026 Reality Labs operating losses to remain similar to 2025." (Item 1A)
  "We may not be successful in our artificial intelligence initiatives, which could adversely affect our business, reputation, or financial results." (Item 1A)
META-r4 | Regulation, privacy, and youth laws | Privacy, content, competition, and youth-protection laws in the US, EU, and elsewhere could force product changes, fines, or limits on advertising, including an FTC consent order and EU rules on ad models.
  "Our business is subject to complex and evolving U.S. and foreign laws and regulations regarding privacy, data use, data combination, data protection, content, AI, competition, youth, safety, consumer protection, advertising, e-commerce, and other matters." (Item 1A)
META-r5 | Litigation | Meta faces numerous class actions and government suits, including youth-related, privacy, antitrust, copyright, and securities claims, which could lead to large damages or required changes.
  "We are involved in numerous class action lawsuits and other litigation matters that are expensive and time consuming, and, if resolved adversely, could harm our business, financial condition, or results of operations." (Item 1A)
  "We are currently, and expect to be in the future, party to patent, trademark, and copyright lawsuits and other intellectual property rights claims that are expensive and time consuming and, if resolved adversely, could have a significant impact on our business, financial condition, or results of operations." (Item 1A)
META-r6 | Security and misuse | Meta is a prominent target for cyber-attacks and misuse of user data, and AI tools add new vulnerabilities.
  "Security breaches, improper access to or disclosure of our data or user data, other hacking and phishing attacks on our systems, or other cyber incidents could harm our reputation and adversely affect our business." (Item 1A)
META-r7 | Infrastructure and supply chain | Meta depends on third-party data center services and a small number of component manufacturers, often concentrated in Asia, for technical infrastructure and consumer hardware.
  "A substantial portion of our technical infrastructure is provided by third parties. Any disruption or failure in the services we receive from these providers could harm our ability to handle existing or increased traffic and could significantly harm our business." (Item 1A)
  "The manufacturing of our consumer hardware products depends on a small number of third parties, often with significant operations in a single region such as Asia." (Item 1A)
META-r8 | Competition | Meta faces competition for users, marketers, developers, and AI talent from many companies, some with greater resources, and platform owners such as Apple and Google can favor their own products.
  "Some of our current and potential competitors may have greater resources, experience, or stronger competitive positions in certain product segments, geographic regions, or user demographics than we do." (Item 1A)
  "For example, each of Apple and Google have integrated competitive products with iOS and Android, respectively." (Item 1A)
META-r9 | Controlled company and dual-class control | Mark Zuckerberg controls a majority of voting power through Class B shares, so Class A holders have limited influence over corporate matters.
  "This concentrated control will limit or preclude your ability to influence corporate matters for the foreseeable future." (Item 1A)
